papers.canonical_title: MAVE: Reconstructing Editable 3D Blockouts from Film Shots
papers.abstract: Animated 3D blockouts support previsualization and provide structural conditions for video generation, but manually reconstructing them from reference videos is costly. MAVE is a video-to-blockout framework combining metric observation, agentic modeling, and evidence-based verification. It recovers cameras, human motion, and geometric evidence; an agent constructs an editable Blender environment; programmatic checks report inconsistencies to guide refinement. Outputs are editable Blender scenes and frame-aligned blockout videos.

events.evidence: arXiv metadata records version 1 published on 17 Nov 2026.

source_records.evidence: Listing attention lead and canonical abstract.

papers.screening_reason: The paper demonstrates an LLM agent operating on an editable Blender graphics environment: it generates edit programs that update a scene, queries evidence, and uses verification feedback to refine the reconstruction.
screening_evidence: Abstract, p.1: an agent constructs an editable environment and programmatic checks guide refinement.
Section 3.2, p.5: Blender executes agent-generated edit programs B_n=Apply(B_{n-1},e_n).
Section 3.2-3.3, pp.5-6: query-edit-verify loop and checks against video/geometric evidence control later edits.

task.evidence: The task is video-to-editable 3D blockout reconstruction and scene modeling.

input_form.evidence: Given a film-shot video V, the method reconstructs a blockout scene.

output.evidence: Outputs are editable Blender scenes and aligned blockout videos.

model_type.evidence: An LLM-based agent generates edit programs; multiple LLM agents are evaluated.

model_training.locator: Section 4.1, p.6; LLM Usage Statement p.10
model_training.evidence: The paper reports evaluated agent backends but does not report training or adaptation of the decision-making models for this task.

planning.evidence: The paper specifies a query-edit-verify policy and operation selection, but does not define an explicit task-plan representation.
planning.reasoning: Because the loop policy is explicit but no plan object or hard-coded plan degree is described, PO labels are not safely assignable.

workflow.evidence: Scene construction proceeds through repeated query, edit, render/inspect, and verify iterations.

update_strategy.evidence: Agent-generated edit programs update the current scene; verification inconsistencies trigger further edits or explicit justifications.
update_strategy.reasoning: Edits are local scene updates and feedback can change subsequent operation choices, supporting Local Patch and Replanning.

verifier.evidence: Verification tools evaluate reconstruction against measured video and geometric evidence.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Checks report depth conflicts, uncovered evidence, occlusion violations, penetration, support, and completeness issues as diagnostics.

feedback_observation.evidence: Observations include structural measurements and diagnostic renderings/scene consistency checks.

memory_time.evidence: R_{n-1} records previous queries, edits, and verification feedback within the iterative run.
memory_time.reasoning: The retained record is within-run state, so it is Short-Term Memory rather than cross-run Long-Term Memory.

memory_reach.evidence: The state record conditions the single agent's next operation.
memory_reach.reasoning: No shared multi-agent or cross-run memory is described; classify as Local Memory.

graphics_software.evidence: The method adds metric observation, evidence querying, and verification tools around Blender for agentic scene construction.
graphics_software.reasoning: The underlying environment is Blender, while the paper supplies an agent-facing adapter/tool layer, matching Agent-Adapted.

tools.evidence: The workflow uses geometric recovery/perception, Blender graphics edits, and static geometric/video consistency validators.

resources.evidence: The agent receives a task description and tool documentation; no reusable asset library is reported for the principal loop.

representation.evidence: Edit programs are code, scene primitives and characters are geometry, and final aligned blockout videos are rendered pixels/media.

papers.contribution: MAVE combines metric video observation, agentic Blender scene construction, and evidence-based verification for editable 3D blockout reconstruction, with MAVEBench and MAVEData-3K.
papers.limitations: The paper relies on recovered camera/human representations and pseudo-depth evidence; verification improves results but does not eliminate reconstruction ambiguity. The agent's explicit planning representation and training/adaptation status are not reported. Full experiments use film-shot blockouts rather than general graphics environments.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time agentic reconstruction subsystem: an LLM controller edits an editable Blender scene using code and is guided by programmatic geometric/video verification feedback.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: LLM-based agent evaluated with MAVE's tool and evidence interface
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Generates Blender edit programs, queries evidence, and chooses further edits or justifications in a query-edit-verify loop
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Editable Blender 3D blockout scene containing camera, geometry, and rigged human proxies
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The paper states that Blender executes agent-generated edit programs and that verification tools report inconsistencies to guide refinement.

papers.canonical_title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
papers.abstract: CADMAGEDDON is an open-source local agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes. A vision-language model chooses feature structure over named geometric entities, while fitting supplies numerical parameters; tools execute CadQuery or FreeCAD programs and report residual missing or extra geometry for subsequent correction.

events.evidence: arXiv metadata records version 1 published on 17 Nov 2026.

papers.screening_reason: The VLM agent directly operates a CAD environment: it selects named geometric entities and operations, emits executable CAD programs, and uses residual/validity feedback to add, correct, undo, or drop features.
screening_evidence: Abstract, p.1: open-source agent reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and geometric tools support visual reasoning.
Section 3, p.4: VLM chooses structure while tools fit parameters and execute the program.
Sections 3.3-3.5, pp.6-7: command-line tool loop, residual verification, and correction actions.

input_form.evidence: The agent receives a triangle mesh of a single part.

output.evidence: The system returns executable CadQuery or native FreeCAD programs and editable CAD geometry.

model_type.evidence: A vision-language model Qwen3.8-27B makes feature decisions from visual/text tool outputs.

model_training.evidence: The paper uses a single open-weight Qwen3.8-27B and states no trained reconstruction model is needed.

planning.evidence: The loop is one command per turn with tool selection and feature decisions; no separate plan object is described.
planning.reasoning: The agent selects actions without a separately represented plan, so PO-3 is used.

workflow.evidence: It executes a sequential trajectory of inspect, construct, verify, and correct commands.

update_strategy.evidence: Features can be replaced, undone, dropped, mirrored, or patterned; residuals guide further actions.

verifier.evidence: The builder checks CAD validity and computes missing/extra residuals; the environment executes operations.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Residual volume and local surface deviations provide numeric discrepancy/diagnostic evidence.

feedback_observation.evidence: Tool reports and renders expose named geometry, current state, residual missing/extra bodies, and visual distance views.

memory_time.evidence: Recent command outputs, renders, summaries, and saved states persist within a reconstruction run.

memory_reach.evidence: The retained context is used by the single agent across turns; no cross-agent/global memory is reported.
memory_reach.reasoning: The memory is local to the agent-run interaction.

action_type.evidence: The model issues CLI commands and the builder emits/executes CAD code.

graphics_software.evidence: Agent-facing instruments and DSL wrap CadQuery/FreeCAD for interactive reconstruction.
graphics_software.reasoning: The method adds an agent harness to general-purpose CAD environments, so Agent-Adapted applies.

tools.evidence: Geometric detectors/fitting, CAD operations, renders, and residual/validity checks are callable workflow tools.

resources.evidence: The system prompt contains a reconstruction guide and command/tool documentation.

representation.evidence: Executable CAD code and named geometric entities are used; rendered views are observations and editable geometry is the artifact.

papers.contribution: CADMAGEDDON separates structural CAD decisions from numerical fitting: a local VLM agent composes feature operations over named fitted geometry, with executable CadQuery/FreeCAD output and residual-driven correction.
papers.limitations: The method assumes a clean single-part mesh; scan noise, missing regions, assemblies, and design intent beyond literal dimensions remain unresolved. It uses up to 30 or 60 model calls and is slower than single-pass learned models. Benchmark comparisons vary in input modality and subset.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time agentic CAD reconstruction subsystem: a VLM controller chooses feature structure and correction actions while geometric tools fit parameters and validate the editable CAD artifact.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: Qwen3.8-27B vision-language model in the CADMAGEDDON command loop
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Selects named planes, profiles, operations, and corrections; issues one CAD command per turn and can undo/drop/replace features
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Editable CadQuery or native FreeCAD parametric CAD program and resulting solid
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The paper explicitly states that the model chooses feature structure, tools emit and execute CAD programs, and residuals guide the next decision.

papers.canonical_title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
papers.abstract: MillBill separates machining decisions from geometric execution and verification. Given a B-rep part, stock, and material, a locally hosted language model proposes operations and cutting parameters; a geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, measures deviations, and returns feedback for plan refinement.

events.evidence: arXiv metadata records version 1 published on 17 Nov 2026.

papers.screening_reason: The language-model controller directly selects machining actions on a CAD/CAM graphics representation and receives simulated geometric feedback that changes subsequent plans.
screening_evidence: Abstract, p.1: model proposes operations/cutting parameters; harness generates toolpaths, simulates removal, and returns feedback.
Sections 3.3-3.6, pp.4-6: ReAct agents revise plans, harness executes/ verifies, deviations return to the model, and fixes are proposed.

task.evidence: The principal subsystem plans and simulates physical machining of a CAD part; the graphics purpose is physical/CAM simulation.

input_form.evidence: Input is a STEP B-rep target part, stock, material, and optional drawing notes.

output.evidence: The workflow exposes structured machining plans, G-code programs, and simulated workpiece state.

model_type.evidence: Qwen3.8-27B language model ReAct agents make process-sequence and tool-selection decisions.

model_training.evidence: The paper explicitly says an off-the-shelf open model makes decisions and no training on machining plans/toolpaths is needed.

planning.evidence: A fixed harness prepares an initial plan; three ReAct sub-agents retrieve knowledge, revise process sequence, and select tools/parameters.
planning.reasoning: Planning is hybrid: reference/setup procedures are fixed while the language model revises operation choices and parameters, supporting PO-2.

workflow.evidence: Knowledge retrieval sub-agents run concurrently, while setup-wise plan-execute-verify-refine cycles are sequential.

update_strategy.evidence: Harness applies direct corrections/rest finishing, model proposes minimal fixes, plan is rebuilt, and best of up to three builds is kept.

verifier.evidence: Geometric simulation, gouge/safety checks, and surface deviation measurement verify every program.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Acc_tau is a numeric score; deviations are diagnosed by feature/operation; builds are ranked and the best retained.

feedback_observation.evidence: Feedback includes simulated workpiece structural state, excess/gouge regions, and execution/safety issues.

memory_time.evidence: Agent stages share current plan, operation state, and prior build feedback within one part run.
memory_time.reasoning: No cross-run persistence is described; this is within-run short-term state.

memory_reach.evidence: The local planner/harness loop uses the retained state; no global cross-agent memory is reported.
memory_reach.reasoning: Use Local Memory for the principal controller loop.

action_type.evidence: Agents return structured JSON operation plans and call harness tools; harness emits G-code.

graphics_software.evidence: The method adds an agent/harness layer around FreeCAD CAM and geometric simulation.
graphics_software.reasoning: The graphics environment is general-purpose FreeCAD/CAM with an agent-facing adapter, so Agent-Adapted.

tools.evidence: AAGNet perception, CAM graphics operations, toolpath generation, simulation/solver validation, static safety checks, and execution utilities are used.

resources.evidence: The workflow retrieves machining guidelines, rules, thread tables, material knowledge, and tool-library data; it also uses reference operation sequences.

representation.evidence: Plans/G-code are code and structured specifications, B-rep/workpiece are geometry, and simulated removal is dynamic state.

papers.contribution: MillBill separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification: a local language-model controller proposes operation sequences, tools, and parameters, while a geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, scores deviations, and feeds corrections back.
papers.limitations: MillBill is limited to indexed three-axis machining from six principal directions; workholding, machine travel, tool-holder collisions, tool deflection, wear, vibration, thread verification, and real-machine effects are not modeled. It is evaluated on 100 parts from one public library and one run per part.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time agentic CAM planning and refinement subsystem: the language model chooses machining actions over a B-rep/CAM environment, while geometric simulation provides loop feedback.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Revises operation sequence, cutter selection, cutting parameters, and minimal corrective fixes through harness tool calls
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: B-rep CAD part, FreeCAD CAM job, generated toolpaths/G-code, and simulated workpiece
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The paper explicitly states that the model makes machining decisions, the harness generates/executes toolpaths, and deviations are returned for plan refinement.

papers.canonical_title: CutAgent: Creative-Gene-Driven Planning and Experience-Guided Self-Refinement for High-CTR E-commerce Advertising Video Creation
papers.abstract: CutAgent is a dual-agent framework for e-commerce advertising video creation. GeneAgent maps product text and images to a structured creative gene of narrative units and production rules. VideoAgent retrieves prior failure-correction experiences, plans shots, retrieves clips, synthesizes narration/subtitles/music, renders a timeline, and runs an evaluation-diagnosis-revision-verification loop that writes verified corrections to long-term memory.

events.evidence: ArXiv metadata records version 1 published on 17 Nov 2026.

papers.screening_reason: CutAgent demonstrates agents making structured planning, retrieval, editing, and rendering decisions over advertising video artifacts, with explicit visual/audio evaluation and iterative correction.
screening_evidence: Abstract, p.1: GeneAgent plans creative genes; VideoAgent coordinates production and reflection.
Sections 3.1-3.3, pp.3-7: structured plan, timeline rendering, evaluation-diagnosis-revision-verification, and memory write-back.
Section B.5, p.15: revisions alter clips, voice-over, duration, or music and re-execute affected modules.

task.evidence: Principal task is planning and producing short advertising videos with ordered narrative units and temporal shots.

input_form.evidence: Product attributes, review text, and main/detail product images are provided.

output.evidence: GeneAgent outputs structured creative genes/storyboards; VideoAgent renders complete advertising videos.

model_type.evidence: GeneAgent is a VLM and VideoAgent is an LLM-driven production agent with multimodal retrieval and rendering tools.

model_training.evidence: GeneAgent uses high-CTR supervised fine-tuning and CTR-guided GRPO; VideoAgent's task-time model configuration is separately described.

planning.evidence: GeneAgent explicitly emits an ordered creative gene before clip selection, and VideoAgent expands it into an executable shot-by-shot storyboard.

workflow.evidence: The system follows Plan–Execute–Self-Evolve: gene planning, video production, then reflection and revision.

update_strategy.evidence: Reflection revises only affected clips, voice-over, duration, or music and re-executes relevant modules; memory stores verified corrections.

verifier.evidence: An evaluator produces six-dimensional scores and temporally grounded evidence; verification re-evaluates the revised video.

feedback_assessment.evidence: NQ, SPC, VSC, MQA, MSS, and TB scores diagnose deficient decisions and determine acceptance.

feedback_observation.evidence: Feedback is grounded in video frames, shot intervals, audio/subtitle segments, and editing elements; execution failures are localized to production modules.

memory_time.evidence: Verified failure-correction experiences are retained and reused across future products without parameter updates.

memory_reach.evidence: Memory is shared across products through category shards and gene matching, rather than restricted to one shot or one call.

action_type.evidence: Agents emit structured creative genes/storyboards and invoke retrieval, TTS, BGM, and rendering tools.

graphics_software.evidence: The system adds agent-facing retrieval, TTS, music matching, subtitle, and ffmpeg timeline tooling around general video assets.
graphics_software.reasoning: The environment is an agent-adapted production pipeline rather than a dedicated graphics-native agent environment.

tools.evidence: Video retrieval/perception, clip/audio/timeline operations, ffmpeg execution, and static/quality checks are callable components.

resources.evidence: The workflow accesses product clip pools, historical failure-correction examples, production rules, and audio/video assets.

representation.evidence: Creative genes/storyboards are structured layouts/specifications; rendered videos are pixels/media; learned state includes the trained GeneAgent policy.

papers.contribution: CutAgent separates conversion-oriented creative planning from video production using a structured creative gene, then adds reflection-based local revision and category/gene-conditioned long-term experience reuse.
papers.limitations: The pipeline depends on retrieved product-specific clip pools and automated multimodal evaluation; the paper notes that VSC is a relative signal because evaluator spatial reasoning is weak. The principal production agent is complex and its learned components are trained on proprietary-scale e-commerce data, limiting direct transferability. Retrieved footage cannot cover a shot when suitable material is absent.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time agentic advertising-video production subsystem (VideoAgent), with GeneAgent training and long-term memory treated as supporting phases rather than mixed into the controller's output fields.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Generates a structured creative gene, expands it into shot scripts, retrieves assets, renders the timeline, and revises affected production modules from temporally grounded evaluation feedback
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: E-commerce advertising video timeline, including clips, narration, subtitles, music, and transitions
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The paper explicitly describes Plan–Execute–Self-Evolve, timeline rendering, and evaluation-diagnosis-revision-verification over the rendered video.

papers.canonical_title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing
papers.abstract: ConserveEdit is an editor-agnostic controller for iterative image editing. It compiles a source-anchored edit contract, composes frozen-editor candidates through an authorized mask, audits progress, protected-content drift, and quality as separate gates, and commits or rolls back candidates with logged repairs.

events.evidence: ArXiv metadata records version 1 published on 17 Nov 2026.

papers.screening_reason: The paper demonstrates a controller that operates on image-editing artifacts at task time: it chooses and commits/rolls back candidate edits against a persistent source contract, with explicit graphics artifact targets and programmatic feedback.
screening_evidence: Abstract, p.1: editor-agnostic controller treats each refinement step as a transaction against a source-image contract.
Sections 3.2-3.3, pp.3-4: candidate image edits are masked, audited, committed, or rolled back.
Section 4, pp.5-8: experiments with frozen Qwen-Image-Edit and MagicBrush image-edit artifacts.

task.evidence: The task is iterative instruction-based image editing with preservation constraints.

input_form.evidence: A source image and free-form instruction are inputs; MagicBrush also supplies edit masks.

output.evidence: The controller returns committed edited images or the source after abstention/rollback.

model_type.evidence: ConserveEdit itself uses no LLM or MLLM; it uses fixed formulas, detectors, segmentation, face, OCR, and frozen image editors.

model_training.evidence: The controller is not trained; frozen executor and fixed evaluators are used.

planning.evidence: The controller follows a fixed algorithm: choose an unsatisfied clause, propose candidates, audit, commit or repair.
planning.reasoning: Planning is entirely specified by the transactional algorithm, corresponding to PO-1.

workflow.evidence: Iterations proceed sequentially over current image state and decision log.

update_strategy.evidence: Masked local commits, rollback on rejection, repair, and lexicographic candidate selection are explicit.

verifier.evidence: Fixed descriptors, masks, progress predicates, quality score, and drift audits decide feasibility.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Drift and quality are numeric scores; clause/progress and feasibility tests diagnose violated conditions and produce binary commit/reject decisions.

feedback_observation.evidence: Observations include pixel/feature drift, masks, image quality, and protected-entity/scene state.

memory_time.evidence: Persistent contract, cumulative support, current image, and decision log persist across iterations of one run.
memory_time.reasoning: The paper does not describe reuse across separate runs; classify the retained controller state as Short-Term Memory.

memory_reach.evidence: State is consumed by the single controller loop; no shared multi-agent memory is described.

action_type.evidence: The controller invokes a frozen editor, mask composition, audits, and repair operations.

graphics_software.evidence: The controller wraps frozen Qwen-Image-Edit/FLUX editors with a source-anchored transaction interface.
graphics_software.reasoning: The editor is adapted with an agent-facing controller and auditing layer, matching Agent-Adapted.

tools.evidence: Frozen image editing is the graphics operation; Grounding DINO/SAM, CLIP/DINO descriptors, face/OCR checks, and quality audits are callable components.

resources.evidence: The controller uses a persistent edit contract and explicit preservation/quality rules.

representation.evidence: The state and output are image pixels; masks/contracts encode structured 2D layout/support information.

papers.contribution: ConserveEdit treats each refinement as a source-anchored transaction with provable invariance and an iteration-independent drift bound, using separate progress, drift, and quality gates plus rollback and logged repair.
papers.limitations: Guarantees apply only to the grounded support and selected descriptors; poor grounding is the main bottleneck. The paper evaluates one frozen editor and MagicBrush, uses fixed-formula predicates rather than an MLLM judge, and reports abstention/seam failures and no human preference study. The controller can preserve the wrong content if descriptors or masks miss a causal dependency.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time graphics-editing controller and acceptance subsystem around a frozen image editor; no learned agentic decision model is used by ConserveEdit itself.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: ConserveEdit transactional controller around frozen Qwen-Image-Edit/FLUX executors
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Selects candidate edits, commits feasible masked transactions, or rolls back and repairs based on source-anchored progress/drift/quality audits
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: 2D image artifact and protected source content
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: The controller explicitly composes image candidates through an authorized mask and commits only when separate image-edit tests pass.
